commands.description: normalize + verify the ESM-only package shape

metadata.description: The nested case, ng-packagr flavour. dist/packages/dbx-web is ONE npm package with several entry points, not several packages: `table`, `docs`, `calendar`, `mapbox` and `style-demo` compile INTO this directory and are named by this package's own dist `exports`. So this target is the sole deliverable and the sole owner of the directory, and those entry points deliberately have no build target of their own -- there is nothing they could publish.  Unlike the rollup families, the secondaries are not listed here at all: ng-packagr's discoverPackages globs `**/ng-package.json` under this package and builds every match as a secondary entry point, so `dbx-web:build-base` ALONE already produces all five. dbx-web-eslint is the one real edge, because it is rollup-built (which is why complete-dbx-web-build.sh has to whitelist `!eslint/package.json` in the generated .npmignore) and because ng-packagr's deleteDestPath wipes this whole directory first -- so it has to be ordered after build-base, not merely alongside it.  What changed: the sequential `npx nx run <target>:build-base:production` shell-outs became dependsOn EDGES. Each was a separate Nx process with its own task graph, so nothing deduped. The `:production` suffix is not lost -- a TargetDependencyConfig has no `configuration` field, but Nx's resolveConfiguration falls back to the target's `defaultConfiguration`, which is `production`. `parallel: false` STAYS: two post-steps remain and they are ordered (the shell script writes the .npmignore that finalize-esm-exports.mjs then reads alongside package.json).  Outputs stay the whole directory, which is correct HERE precisely because this task is its only writer: the cache payload is always complete, so the restore that remove()s the directory always puts all of it back.  Outputs were also NARROWED to just the directory. The extra entries (_index.scss, LICENSE, `**/*.scss`) were all SUBSETS of it, but declaring more than one output flips Nx's cache RESTORE from directory mode to file mode: the native expandOutputs returns a single entry for a lone directory -- so copyFilesFromCache remove()s the whole directory and replaces it -- but ENUMERATES that directory's files once another output is present, and a per-file remove+copy cannot delete anything the payload does not contain. That mattered the moment build-base became a task in this same graph: build-base's payload legitimately contains the intermediate src/ tree that complete-dbx-web-build.sh deletes, so restoring build-base (directory mode) and then build (file mode) left a stray dist/packages/dbx-web/src behind on every cache hit. One output, one writer, one complete payload.

`^build`, not `^build-base`. @nx/js remaps @dereekb/* imports to the dist DIRECTORY, so TypeScript reads that directory's package.json `exports` to resolve them -- and the dependency's own `build` is what finalizes those exports. Declared explicitly rather than inherited from the `@nx/angular:package` targetDefault in nx.json so the edge is visible where it matters; the value is the same.  This one target builds the primary entry point AND every secondary (table, docs, calendar, mapbox, style-demo), because ng-packagr discovers them from their nested ng-package.json files.
